QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_8

question.text: A PE secondary intermediary pitches Brahmaputra Growth Partners on a transaction where the GP rolls TWO mature portfolio companies out of the existing fund into a new vehicle backed by a secondary buyer — LPs choose to cash out or roll. This structure is BEST described as:

answer.text: A recapitalisation of the fund via dividend recap
A strip sale of minority interests

explanation.text: The Logic: A Continuation Vehicle moves selected portfolio assets from the original fund into a new fund vehicle managed by the same GP, with a secondary buyer providing liquidity and legacy LPs given a cash-or-roll option. Multiple assets being rolled = MULTI-ASSET CV. Single asset = single-asset CV. The Trap: LP-led is an investor-side stake sale with no asset reshuffle. Strip sale moves only a pro-rata slice of each asset. Dividend recap is a leverage-up of a single portfolio company for cash distribution — not a fund-level secondary. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C introduces GP-led secondaries specifically because XIX-A/B do not touch them. XXI-B (PM) does not cover private-market liquidity tools. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before running a CV, commission a fairness opinion and a conflict-of-interest waiver via the LPAC. Skipping these invites a SEBI examination letter and lasting reputational damage even if the economics work.
